newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse to issue corporate governance code.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse to issue corporate governance code.

text.p: The Brussels Stock Exchange said on Wednesday it had set up a committee charged with issuing a code on corporate governance to Belgium's listed companies.
The code will contain non-binding recommendations on relations between directors, managers and shareholders; board membership; and company information policy.
The responsibility of institutional investors will also be covered, the bourse said in a statement.

The committee will be chaired by former Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL) chief executive officer Daniel Cardon de Lichtbuer. The code will only be issued after an unspecified period of consultation with Belgium's financial community.

Corporate governance has become a hot topic in Belgium following the merger this year between Lyonnaise des Eaux and Suez led to the government insisting the new French group would not dominate the board of Belgian utility unit Tractebel, which controls the country's gas and electricity sector.
Tractebel adjusted the composition of its board to meet the government concerns.

Other companies are following suit. Holding company Lonrho Continental said on Wednesday it would also adjust the composition of its board to reflect its own corporate governance guidelines following a decision by its controlling shareholder, Lonrho Plc, to withdraw from the company.

Some companies however are opposed to any corporate governance code being foisted upon them. Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert told its annual general meeting earlier this year it would oppose any attempts to impose a code upon it.
